claims.text: FeCoNiCrAl powder with a 15–45 μm particle-size range produces high-quality coatings under HVAF-M3 conditions.
Standard HVAF-i7 processing of 15–45 μm FeCoNiCrAl powder produces acceptable coating quality but inadequate thickness.
Reducing the HVAF-i7 nozzle-to-substrate distance to approximately 300–350 mm will increase in-flight particle velocity.
Higher in-flight particle velocity increases particle kinetic energy at impact.
Greater impact kinetic energy improves particle flattening, deformation, and inter-particle bonding.
Improved particle deformation and bonding will produce a denser and thicker FeCoNiCrAl deposit.
Reducing spray distance and increasing velocity shortens in-flight residence time and thereby minimizes oxidation.
Spray distance can affect the oxide content and phase behavior of HVOF-sprayed high-entropy-alloy coatings.
Conventional MCrAlY bond coats show a slight deposition-efficiency gain at higher particle velocity.
Nozzle-specific optimum spray distances for the prior MCrAlY work were approximately 300 and 350 mm.
The intervention will produce a significantly thicker and adherent FeCoNiCrAl bond coat than standard HVAF-i7 processing.
The thicker coating will retain minimal as-sprayed oxidation.
The coating produced by the intervention will retain durability during high-temperature service.
The intervention will remain effective when coating internal diameters of approximately 120 mm.
An excessive velocity increase could cause overheating or phase instability and counteract the intervention's benefits.
The hypothesis is falsified if the reduced-distance group fails to achieve a statistically significant thickness increase exceeding 10% without deterioration of oxidation or adhesion performance.
